title: From Literature to ‘ReWA’: Discussing Reproductive Well-being in HCI

bias_targets.methodology: Systematic literature review and thematic mapping of 147 HCI and social computing papers to quantify the underrepresentation of men, non-binary, and LGBTQ+ individuals, and to critique the default assumption of cisgender women in reproductive health technologies.

Analyzing the geographic distribution of research (Global North vs. Global South) and evaluating how reproductive technologies and AI models rely on 'one-size-fits-all', Western-centric datasets, norms, and temporalities.

Reviewing existing literature to identify structural exclusions and barriers faced by low-income, migrant, non-English speaking, and low-literacy populations in accessing reproductive digital health interventions.
